# v2.56-dev Release Notes

## New: Offerings are now company-scoped

Offerings used to be global — every offering was visible to everyone, and every
API key could read them all. Now **each offering belongs to a company**, so a
company has its own set of offerings that only people (and API keys) with access
to that company can see or manage.

### Changed

- **Every offering belongs to one company.** When you create an offering you now
  pick which company it's for, and the offering (its specialisations and
  supporting-training requirements) is only visible to users granted that
  company. The public Offerings pages, the sidebar list, and the read-only public
  API all filter to the companies you're allowed to see.

- **Names are unique per company, not globally.** Two different companies can now
  each have an offering with the same name.

- **Company Admins can manage their own offerings.** Offerings management used to
  be SuperAdmin-only. Now a company Admin can create, edit, import, and delete the
  offerings for the companies they administer (SuperAdmins still see everything).
  The admin list shows a company badge in the "All companies" view, and the New
  Offering and Import dialogs ask which company to use.

- **Import and export carry the company.** The offerings export now includes a
  Company column; the import loads all rows into the single company you choose,
  and only ever replaces that company's offerings — never another company's
  identically-named one.

### Notes

- **This release includes a database migration.** Any offerings you already have
  are automatically assigned to your **oldest company** during the upgrade; you
  can reassign each one afterward in Admin → Offerings.
- Backups carry the company assignment. Restoring a full backup preserves it;
  restoring a **config** backup (which doesn't include companies) lands offerings
  on the target's oldest company, ready to reassign.
- No configuration changes required.
